articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 4
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Steelers-Browns game.

-->

Week 4 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ CAR

Six touchdowns in three games is quite the feat. It's LaDainian Tomlinson stuff (2006).
 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs LAC

The league leader in fantasy points seems unstoppable, regardless of matchup.
 3. Josh Allen, QB1 vs NE

He has rushed for two touchdowns in each game. Can the Patriots stop him?
 4. Bijan Robinson, RB2 @ NO

He has scored more than 30 points in two of three games. 
 5. Lamar Jackson, QB2 vs TEN

The 50 rushing yards from the Week 3 win are a terrific sign.
 6. Ja'Marr Chase, WR2 vs JAX

 7. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR3 @ CAR

 8. Puka Nacua, WR4 @ PHI

A hip injury has cost him two games. At least the Rams play at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.
 9. Jonathan Taylor, RB3 @ WSH

More than 20 touches each week, which is nice when he doesn't score a TD or two.
 10. Derrick Henry, RB4 vs TEN

You know he always wants to shine against his former Titans teammates. 
 11. Kenneth Walker III, RB5 @ LV

The volume was down a bit, but he scores TDs. Note: Chiefs are on a bye in Week 5. Plan ahead!
 12. Christian McCaffrey, RB6 vs DEN

The 49ers are keeping his volume well in check. It's a tough matchup with the Broncos this week.
 13. Brock Purdy, QB3 vs DEN

 14. Patrick Mahomes, QB4 @ LV

 15. Tyler Shough, QB5 vs ATL

 16. Trevor Lawrence, QB6 @ CIN

His investors could have used the rushing TD he gave to a teammate on Sunday.
 17. Justin Jefferson, WR5 vs MIA

An ankle injury could cost him Week 4. It's too early to panic about the team's QBs.
 18. Chris Olave, WR6 vs ATL

 19. Ashton Jeanty, RB7 vs KC

 20. James Cook III, RB8 vs NE

The argument that his QB steals the rushing TDs doesn't work. Cook is great.
 21. Jalen Hurts, QB7 vs LAR

Mild concern over a disappointing Monday effort. The Rams visit Philly Sunday. That's not great, either.
 22. Joe Burrow, QB8 vs JAX

 23. Bryce Young, QB9 vs DET

 24. Matthew Stafford, QB10 @ PHI

If a third-string QB can light up the Eagles, what do you think Stafford can do?
 25. CeeDee Lamb, WR7 @ HOU

Some may try to fade top Cowboys against the Texans, but that is a mistake. 
 26. Drake London, WR8 @ NO

Any worries about his production ended in Week 3. London dominated the Packers.

One of the best backups in the business remains a solid investment this week.

articles.headline: Source - Bengals cut Ke'Shawn Williams after costly muffed punt
articles.description: The Cincinnati Bengals cut WR Ke'Shawn Williams after he muffed a punt that eventually led to the Pittsburgh Steelers' 30-27 win, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Earlier Tuesday, Cincinnati signed WR Mitch Tinsley, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals are making changes following their first loss of the season on Sunday. 

They've released Ke'Shawn Williams, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, after the wide receiver muffed a fourth-quarter punt that led to the game-winning field goal in Cincinnati's 30-27 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The move comes on the heels of Cincinnati bringing back wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Bengals needed depth at wide receiver because of injuries to Andrei Iosivas, who is on injured reserve following thumb surgery, and rookie Colbie Young's left knee injury that will keep him out for at least one week.

On Monday, Bengals coach Zac Taylor indicated that a move was imminent following the costly late-game turnover.

"I'm not at that decision today on what exactly that's going to look like, but that's a conversation we'll have," Taylor said post-game when asked about Williams' role moving forward.

The two transactions also highlighted what was a notable training camp battle this summer.

Williams made the team's initial 53-man roster over Tinsley, who had a breakout training camp in 2025 and spent all of last season with the Bengals. Williams started four of his 17 appearances and caught eight passes for 116 yards and two touchdowns.

Tinsley was among the team's final cuts and was signed to the Houston Texans' practice squad.

articles.headline: Jerry Jones: 'No explanation' for Cowboys coaches' mistakes
articles.description: Jerry Jones says he believes errors in game management by his coaching staff cost the Cowboys a victory over the Ravens.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is leaving little doubt that he believes errors in game management by his coaching staff in the final seconds of a 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens cost his team the victory.

Speaking on his radio show Tuesday, Jones was asked what explanations there were for leaving enough seconds on the clock after a tying field goal for a defensive breakdown to put the Ravens in position for the winning kick.

"There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," Jones said. "Let's be sure that we all understand that. They [coaches] don't have one that they're satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time. There's no question about it. So there is no explanation. But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again."

Trailing 31-28, the Cowboys had a first down at the Baltimore 2-yard line with 23 seconds left when Dak Prescott threw incomplete into the end zone.

After a false-start penalty against tight end Luke Schoonmaker, Prescott scrambled to the Baltimore 5, and coach Brian Schottenheimer called his final timeout with 14 seconds remaining.

The coach, who is also the playcaller, instructed Prescott to either throw a quick out to receiver George Pickens or throw the ball away, based on the amount of time left and with no ability to stop the clock. Prescott didn't wait long to choose the throwaway, and the play lasted just four seconds.

There were seven seconds remaining after Brandon Aubrey's game-tying field goal, and the Dallas defense left a gap at just about the exact spot of the target line for a Baltimore field goal. Lamar Jackson completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers and got the timeout called with a second to go, and Tyler Loop made the 56-yard field goal.

Schottenheimer is in his second season as a head coach after 25 years as an NFL assistant. Christian Parker is a 34-year-old making his debut as a defensive coordinator. Both will be under considerable scrutiny from fans and pundits going forward, and perhaps from their own front office.

"We will be better from this experience that we had with Baltimore and what happened to us at the end of the game," Jones said. "A win would have given you another way of couching it as far as having growth and enthusiasm for having won a game like that because we did come back and we came back in an impressive way. All of that makes us realize we really are just at the beginning of what I hope is an exciting year for us."

The Cowboys (1-2) got a break in the NFC East when the two-time defending division champion Philadelphia Eagles lost to the Chicago Bears and backup quarterback Case Keenum on Monday night.

Dallas visits the Houston Texans (0-3) on Sunday. The New York Giants, who will be without quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the regular season because of a knee injury, are tied with the Eagles atop the division at 2-1. The Washington Commanders, like the Cowboys, are 1-2.

articles.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Purdy joins top five QBs, Sadiq impresses among TEs
articles.description: Need a quick free agent pickup -- or roster overhaul -- after Week 3? These rankings are designed to help.
articles.body:
Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize the players for their future potential and/or to gauge their value in trade. Eric's top 100 can be found below the positions in this column. 

Quarterback

Rankings changes: It was an odd Week 3 for quarterbacks, as stalwarts Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson were not among the top 10 fantasy scorers, but Case Keenum was. Four of the top five scorers (Sam Darnold, Geno Smith, Jacoby Brissett, Keenum) did not enter the week among our top 20 in these rankings. Darnold and Brissett force their way in. The top 10 sees minimal change, although Brock Purdy rises to fourth and Matthew Stafford is thriving. Drake Maye and Justin Herbert continue to slide. Baker Mayfield (thumb) slides due to injury, though he will return soon. Now with the New York Giants, J.J. McCarthy enters the rankings, barely.

Running back

Rankings changes: The season is over for Dolphins star De'Von Achane (knee), so Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright (though barely) enter the rankings. Achane leaving the top 10 is the major rankings adjustment, though Jeremiyah Love and Kyren Williams pass Chase Brown to move into RB1 status, and Jaylen Warren and Quinshon Judkins look like potential RB2 options. Patriots TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson, and disappointing David Montgomery, do not.

Wide receiver

Rankings changes: Seahawks star Jaxon Smith-Njigba, averaging better than 34 points per game, takes the No. 1 overall spot. The top 10 at wide receiver sees minor adjustment, with injured Puka Nacua (hip) and Nico Collins (hamstring) falling a bit, though perhaps each will play in Week 4. Drake London looks like a WR1 again, and top Packers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden feel reliable. Tre' Harris, Kalif Raymond and Keenan Allen join the rankings.

Tight end

Rankings changes: Welcome back, Brock Bowers! The Las Vegas star led the position with 27.6 points, followed by George Kittle and Harold Fannin Jr. Jets rookie Kenyon Sadiq is a big riser, closing in on TE1 status. Tucker Kraft and Kyle Pitts Sr. continue to slide.

articles.headline: Sources: Giants to release fan favorite Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.description: The Giants are releasing veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr., sources told NFL Network.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are releasing Odell Beckham Jr., sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, after the veteran wide receiver failed to make a significant impact over his first three games back with the team.

Beckham, a longtime fan favorite, was one of the last players to make the Giants' 53-man roster earlier this month after impressing throughout training camp.

But Beckham struggled to earn consistent playing time once the season started and logged only one target over the Giants' first three games.

Beckham, 33, played just six offensive snaps in Sunday's 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans. The three-time Pro Bowler is second in Giants franchise history in receiving yards.

articles.headline: Man City guilty of all charges of Premier League financial breaches
articles.description: Manchester City have been found guilty of all 115 charges of serious breaches of Premier League regulations, the Premier League confirmed in a 1,545-word statement on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Manchester City have been found guilty of all 115 charges of serious breaches of Premier League regulations, the Premier League confirmed in a 1,545-word statement Tuesday.

Richard Masters, the Premier League CEO, said that the findings show that City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade."

City face huge points deductions and fines, with the Premier League holding the ability to issue an ultimate sanction of expulsion from the league.

City, who denied all charges, have until Friday to exercise their right to an appeal.

In its verdict, the independent panel found that City arranged "sham" contracts with commercial partners to artificially inflate their commercial earnings, filed "misstated" accounts to conceal the true nature of their finances and "significantly" breached Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

In its statement, the Premier League said City used "disguised funding schemes" to deceive and mislead the league.

The statement said: "The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club's revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules.

"The consequence of this, as the Commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators. The Commission concluded that 'by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules.'"

Masters, who has been criticized for the length of time taken to bring City to account, said the verdict was a "vindication" of the decision to take action against the club.

"The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period," Masters said. "It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

"It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

articles.headline: NBA preseason: Answering big questions for all 30 teams
articles.description: From LeBron James' fit in Philadelphia to Kawhi Leonard's return to Toronto, we're answering the biggest preseason questions for all 30 teams.
articles.body:
Monday's media day kicked off NBA training camps around the league and offered a first look at several stars in their new homes. The Philadelphia 76ers had perhaps the biggest offseason, adding Jaylen Brown on July 1 and then the league's all-time leading scorer LeBron James before the month was over. But the Sixers aren't the only ones who made big moves.

James' former team, the Los Angeles Lakers, took a big swing in trading for former Jazz center Walker Kessler, and Giannis Antetokounmpo finally found a new home in the Miami Heat. LaMelo Ball is teaming up with Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves, and Ja Morant will look for a fresh start with the Portland Trail Blazers.

Big trades and signings aren't the only noteworthy storylines coming out of the offseason. Will the Detroit Pistons resolve Jalen Duren's contract dispute? How will the San Antonio Spurs rebound after collapsing in the Finals? Our NBA Insiders answer the biggest preseason questions for all 30 teams.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

Will the Hawks build on their strong finish to last season?

To be clear, the Hawks' 51-point loss in their elimination game isn't the strong finish we are referring to. But Atlanta did account for two of the Knicks' three playoff losses, and the Hawks went on a 19-4 run with a plus-13.9 average point differential at the end of the regular season after committing to CJ McCollum in the starting lineup.

Atlanta added to the roster this summer -- drafting Kingston Flemings in the lottery and trading for ring-earning role players Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins -- and is positioned to be aggressive at the trade deadline or next summer, when the Hawks could have about $45 million in salary cap space. -- Tim MacMahon

Boston Celtics

Is Jayson Tatum ready to assume command of the Celtics on the court?

Tatum made it a point to get back on the court before last season ended, proving his Achilles injury couldn't keep him down. The results were mixed in the short term, as his regular-season percentages were down across the board and he sat out Game 7 of the Celtics' first-round series because of left knee discomfort.

Trading Jaylen Brown was a full endorsement of Tatum's ability to take the throttle while retooling to get back to championship status. But is Tatum fully recovered from the injury and ready to assume control? -- Vincent Goodwill

Brooklyn Nets

Can the Nets go from deplorable to dependable?

The Nets invested in a long-term rebuilding plan: think of those first-round picks Sean Marks held onto in the 2025 draft, rather than attempting to aggregate them for impact players. But then lottery reform happened, forcing the Nets to press the fast-forward button in July.

Trading for Julius Randle upgraded their talent, as did drafting another point guard in Mikel Brown Jr.
